Bayes' rule, which describes the probability of an event based on prior knowledge of conditions that might be related to the event, is given by:

\[ P(A|B) = \frac{P(B|A) \cdot P(A)}{P(B)} \]

Here, \( P(A|B) \) is the posterior probability of event \( A \) given that \( B \) is true, \( P(B|A) \) is the likelihood of event \( B \) given that \( A \) is true, \( P(A) \) is the prior probability of event \( A \), and \( P(B) \) is the marginal probability of event \( B \).
